subject: Q4 OKR trajectory: tighten scope and finalize cross-team handoffs
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Q4 OKR trajectory: tighten scope and finalize cross-team handoffs

Team / Sara —

Quick mid-quarter pulse and asks so we can lock the QBR narrative and the dependency owners this week. High-level: the top-line OKR health is mixed and we need to tighten scope on one initiative ("model-packing pilot") so we can guarantee delivery on the platform stability and customer-facing evals that directly impact the Q4 renewal ask.

Status (short):
- OKR: Production latency and reliability for hosted chat — amber. Current 95p token latency target is missed in our largest tenant runs.
- OKR: Model-packing pilot — green on prototype, but needs a sustained infra runway to reach production-grade packaging and regression testing.
- OKR: Evals & quality monitoring — red risk if we don't add labeling capacity; this is the highest customer-impact item for AcmeCorp.

Proposed course (asks):
1) Re-scope: pause non-blocking features in the model-packing pilot (defer autoscaling heuristics) and keep the compatibility work. This reduces required infra capacity by ~35% for the remainder of the quarter.
2) Reassign 0.5 FTE from the pilot to the evals effort (labeling and regression set up) for the next 6 weeks.
3) Karthik: confirm infra can commit the remaining runway and a one-off GPU burst for the test matrix. See attached infra-runbook for the plan.
4) Laura: confirm labeling scope and whether we need an external contractor (estimate of cost/time).
5) Sara: heads up — we'll present the tightened QBR slide and ask for a short decision window during our customer review next week. Anything we should call out in the slide for Acme?

Please reply with ownership confirmations and any objections by EOD 2026-11-07 PST. I attached the current QBR slide deck draft (QBR-draft-v3.pptx) — slide 7 is the OKR trajectory we want to narrate. Drive link to artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBRDraft-Redwood

Short rationale: pushing a small scope change now preserves SLOs and the customer story; letting both pilot and evals run at full scope risks under-delivery on both.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Product, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment: QBR-draft-v3.pptx (presentation, 12 slides)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 18:31:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Q4 OKR trajectory: tighten scope and finalize cross-team handoffs

Irene — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers:
- Infra runway: we can absorb the reduced capacity needs if we defer autoscaling heuristics. We'll need to schedule a controlled GPU burst for the packaging test matrix; estimate: 48–72 GPU hours across two weeks.
- Risks: KV cache sizing and batch pipeline tuning are the primary risks for p95 latency regressions; I'll own mitigation.

I'll attach the infra-runbook describing the burst schedule and rollback plan. If Laura confirms the contractor ask, we can sequence the burst for week of 11/16. Otherwise we'll need to push to late-Nov which makes the QBR story weaker.

Action: I confirm infra ownership for the burst and the rollback plan, pending scheduling confirmation from ops.

-Karthik
Infra Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: infra-runbook.pdf (PDF, 7 pages)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Q4 OKR trajectory: tighten scope and finalize cross-team handoffs

Irene / Karthik —

Thanks — a couple clarifying points from the evals side:
- Success metric: can we add end-to-end 95th token latency under customer load as a secondary metric in the slide? The customer cares about tail latency more than average.
- Labeling: we will need a short-term contractor to hit the labeling throughput for the regression sets. Estimate: 3k labeled examples over 3 weeks. I can source a contractor for ~$12k; if leadership wants to avoid contractor spend, we'll reduce the regression scope and that increases the quality risk.
- SLA exception: if we de-prioritize model-packing features, we should draft a short SLA exception note for AcmeCorp explaining the trade and timeline. I started a draft: SLA-exception-request.docx (attached).

Quote your point so it's explicit: "pushing a small scope change now preserves SLOs and the customer story; letting both pilot and evals run at full scope risks under-delivery on both." I agree.

I'll finalize the labeling estimate and wire the contractor pipeline if we get the green light.

Laura
Director, Customer Success & Evals
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-exception-request.docx (DOCX, 2 pages)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 20:12:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Q4 OKR trajectory: tighten scope and finalize cross-team handoffs

Markus —

Looping you in for a quick decision: team has converged on a plan to reduce scope on non-essential model-packing features and reassign capacity to evals (labeling + regression) to protect the Acme renewal narrative. Karthik can provide the GPU burst; Laura needs approval for a contractor (~$12k) to meet the regression timeline.

Options:
A) Approve the re-scope + contractor spend (recommended) — preserves customer-facing metrics for QBR.
B) Keep both streams at full scope — high risk of missing both targets and a weaker renewal story.

If A is acceptable, we will: confirm infra schedule (Karthik), finalize contractor by 11/10 (Laura), and ship the tightened QBR slide for leadership review on 11/12.

Markus, any preference? Quick thumbs up/down will suffice.

Thanks —
Vivek
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

-- End of thread --
